content.title: About
content.content: Gouda is a semi‑hard cheese originating from the Dutch city of Gouda. Made from cow’s milk, it has a mild nutty flavor and a slightly sweet aroma. The texture is firm yet elastic, and the color ranges from pale yellow to golden.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gouda is one of the oldest cheeses in the Netherlands, with production dating back over 800 years.
The cheese is aged from a few weeks to several years; longer aging yields a stronger taste and a harder texture.
Traditionally Gouda is coated with a wax rind that protects it from drying out.
Some Dutch Gouda develops tiny calcium crystals during aging, giving a pleasant crunchy bite.
Gouda is commonly used in casseroles, sandwiches, and fondue.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium in Gouda supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: The cheese provides high‑quality milk protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Gouda contains vitamin B12, riboflavin and niacin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: In moderate amounts, the cheese supplies beneficial fatty acids that can support heart health.

items.title: Probiotic bacteria
items.content: Fermentation creates beneficial microbes that may help maintain gut flora.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after eating cheese.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Gouda is salted, so those with high blood pressure should monitor portion size.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to casein.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese is calorie‑dense, so it should be consumed in moderation when managing weight.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gouda can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, sandwiches, pastas, and casseroles. It melts well, making it ideal for fondue and pizza. Serve at room temperature to fully appreciate its aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Gouda in the refrigerator, wrapped in wax paper or parchment and then placed in an airtight container. It keeps well for 2–3 months. Discard if mold develops or if it develops an off‑smell.
